orgReasonsEvidence.recurs: 1,646 lessons on disk (720 published, 692 draft, 234 in review: npm run company -- status, 2026-10-25); lane S plans 100 published lessons per two-week cycle (company/ops/projects.json lane-single-card basis).
orgReasonsEvidence.too-big-for-one-context: 14 curricula (content/curriculum/*.json) and 8,260 claims awaiting the fact-checker (company status, 2026-10-25). One lesson fits one context (system3-meta research/bench6/BENCH6.md); the catalogue does not. Held as data for one pooled category-curator, not as 51 manager roles (F-50).
orgReasonsEvidence.independent-checking: Builders never mark their own claims verified (CLAUDE.md; tools/company.mjs claimGates refuses a claim verified by its builder). M6: the independent fact-checker found real errors in 7 of 10 lessons after the builders' own checks passed (system3-meta research/bench6/PREDICTIONS.md). Learner data and a child-safety trigger need a privacy gate (AMD-015).
orgReasonsEvidence.long-horizon: A live product with accounts, a feed and 21 production releases since 2026-10-14 (company/ops/releases.json); the disk is the memory (CLAUDE.md).

sizeReason: 34 roles (33 agents) against the default of 8, falling to about 30 on 2026-11-23. The evidence supports about 30: the 11 roles of the two production flows (curator, builder, interaction-designer, qa, fact, learner, a11y, pedagogy, route, release, design-lead) and the referee owner, because the work recurs at 100 lessons a cycle across 14 curricula and the constitution separates maker from checker at four gates; 4 managers who hold priority and lane budgets; the operator and its auditor; 7 engineers and stewards of a live product with learner accounts and a privacy gate; 2 for learning and metrics; 1 research pool; 2 for personalization (one maker, personalization-engineer, and its independent judge, personalization-eval, now under evaluation-steward) plus growth-designer. The 5 personalization roles with no measured run were parked by F-52 G2 (company/decisions/2026-10-25-founder-f52.md). The 3 left above the reason are dated, as the founder approved: head-of-strategic-initiatives and vp-marketing park at First Light's close on 2026-11-23 (First Light's own release work needs them until then), and rnd-lead parks if F-49 is declined (it holds the open rnd-knots tranche).

baseline.weighed: Benchmark 6 ran the single-agent baseline on this company's work: one vanilla agent (V) with the company's CLAUDE.md, hooks and tools against the many-stage flow (M) on the same 3 cs.systems one-card briefs, scored blind.
baseline.result: V cost $7.19 against $16.66 (43%; about 51% counting its unpriced nested sessions), took 36.5 min against 98, had 0 confirmed S1/S2 defects against 1, 3/3 accepted against 2/3, and won 2 of 3 pairwise. V checked its claims with nested checker sessions it launched itself, which the protocol does not count as independent.
baseline.conclusion: At the size of one lesson the single agent won. The org is kept only for what one agent cannot hold or must not do: the recurring catalogue, the breadth of 14 curricula, and checks independent of the maker (enforced in code, not briefed by the builder). Each item's own flow should look like V: one warm maker running its own checks, then independent checks once (PRINCIPLES.md P2).
baseline.caveats: n = 3 lessons, one model, both arms in parallel on 4 CPUs; M's time includes environment and founder waits.

flows.title: Lane S: single-card lesson (every single-card format)

steps.what: brief: misconception, claims, format, reviewRoute, proposed priority; batches of 10-20
build plus pre-flight; 10-20 briefs per run
npm run check, QA contract record, tools/a11y-scan.mjs
claims, in batches of 50
learner walk of the current version (every lesson until AMD-017 is ratified)
route verdict, tier R only (sensitive, safety, copyright, health, money)
one revision round: one fix, re-run only the failed check, then publish or park
signs the batch launch record with predictions
publishes
approves every deploy

flows.title: Lane M: multi-card sequence (2-4 sub-cards): one warm maker per item, checks once at the end (F-52 G1)
flows.source: company/decisions/2026-10-25-founder-f52.md (G1); company/ops/projects.json lane-multi-card.flow; company/ceo-office/poc-map.md lane 6; manager design-lead. Supersedes the F-50 relay (company/ceo-office/2026-10-25-restructuring-proposal.md section 2c)

steps.what: brief: 2-4 sub-cards, claims, category sensitivities, numbers script

one session owns the item: writes its interaction spec and mockup, then builds, and runs its own checks in its loop (npm run check, the brief's numbers script, QA contract, sequence-probe, reveal-fit, a11y-scan, the 60-second time estimate) and walks every reachable path (skip, mid-animation reveal, settled back)
interaction review of the spec and the built stage, artifact first
automated checks plus sequence probe
claims
learner walk (every item for the first 10)
design review, first 3 items
pairwise against the single-card twin, first 3 items (the cube lesson runs it after publish: founder, 2026-10-25)
one revision round, from its own build notes
batch launch record
publishes
approves every deploy
